title: Day 11 — Prompt → Precise Spec
prompt: Product wants a slugify function for blog URLs. That's the whole ask. Before you write any code, tell me exactly how it should behave — I'm curious what questions you'd pin down first.

clarifications.answer: Only [a-z0-9] survive. Any run of other characters collapses to a single hyphen.
Keep it simple: non-ASCII letters are treated as separators, not transliterated. 'Café' -> 'caf'.
Empty input or all-symbol input yields an empty string.
No max-length requirement for this version.

hints: List every decision the one-sentence ask left open BEFORE writing code — that's the whole exercise.
Think in terms of: which characters survive, and what happens to everything else (runs of them).
One regex does it: replace runs of [^a-z0-9] with '-' on the lowercased string, then strip('-').
